text: Breakpoints in a priority queue.

Slope trick keeps a DP whose value is a convex piecewise-linear function f(x) of one variable, not as an array but as the multiset of its breakpoints (points where the slope changes by 1). Adding |x − a| inserts a at both sides; taking a prefix minimum ("x may only increase") throws away the right side. A priority queue stores the breakpoints, so each step is O(log n).

Classic: make an array non-decreasing with the fewest ±1 changes (P4597). fi(x) = min cost with bi = x. Keep a max-heap: push ai; if the top t > ai, pay t − ai, pop t and push ai again. The answer is the total paid.
Strictly increasing: subtract i from ai first.
Checked against the O(n·V) DP over final values in Python. The heap holds where the slope of f changes; its top is the point where f is smallest.
Other slope-trick moves: adding a constant to all breakpoints (shift), keeping two heaps for both sides with lazy offsets, and merging heaps along a tree for tree versions.
Middle first; opt ranges shrink.

Divide-and-conquer optimisation (分治优化): for f[g][i] = minj<i f[g−1][j] + cost(j, i), when the best j (opt) is monotone in i, compute the middle i first by scanning its whole allowed range of j, then recurse on the left half with j ≤ opt(mid) and on the right half with j ≥ opt(mid). Each layer costs O(n log n) instead of O(n²).

Monotone opt holds when cost satisfies the quadrangle inequality (拓展篇第20章); "sum of the segment squared" does. Splitting into k groups with the smallest Σ (group sum)² is 征途(P4072, which also has a slope-optimisation solution).
Twelve random values split into 4 groups; checked against the O(k n²) DP in Python. The recursion depth is log n and each level of one layer scans O(n) candidates in total.
Heaviest walks of exactly L edges.

Matrix power in the (max, +) semiring (广义矩阵乘法): replace "multiply" by "+" and "add" by "max": C[i][j] = maxk (A[i][k] + B[k][j]). It is still associative, so fast power works (进阶篇第22章). AL[i][j] is the heaviest walk of exactly L edges from i to j; with (min, +) it is the lightest.

Missing edges are −∞ (for max) or +∞ (for min); identity has 0 on the diagonal and −∞ elsewhere. This semiring view is also the engine behind dynamic DP (第21章): a DP step that is "max over choices of a sum" is a (max, +) matrix product.

Bracket plugs on the profile; Hamiltonian cycles.

Plug DP (插头 DP, broken-profile DP on connectivity): process the grid cell by cell; the state is the row of m + 1 "plugs" crossing the boundary between processed and unprocessed cells. To count Hamiltonian cycles (P5056), each plug is 0 (none), 1 (left end of a path) or 2 (right end), like brackets; paths never cross, so the bracket matching tells which ends are joined.

At a cell with left plug L and up plug U: (0,0) start a new path going down and right (1, 2); one plug: continue it down or right; (1,1) or (2,2): join two paths, and the partner bracket of one end changes; (2,1): join simply; (1,2): closes a loop, allowed only at the last free cell. States are stored in a hash map, base 4.

Three grids, checked against a Python DFS that counts Hamiltonian cycles directly (each cycle found twice, once per direction). The bracket search starts at the plug itself, so the plug being changed is found as its own partner's match.

Shift the state by one plug at the start of each row (the right plug of the last cell is always 0). Use 64-bit states once m + 1 plugs need more than 32 bits, and a hand-written hash table if unordered_map is too slow.
